title: Compatible equivariant monoid chart with smooth comparison
statement:
Let $f:(X,M_X)\to(B,M_B)$ be a log smooth morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. A finite group $G$ acts by log automorphisms and $f$ is equivariant. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ with image $\bar b$, assume every element of $G$ fixes $\bar x$, $|G|$ is invertible near $\bar b$, and $G$ acts trivially on the characteristic monoids $\overline M_{X,\bar x}$ and $\overline M_{B,\bar b}$. Choose an integer $N$ divisible by the exponent of $G$, a primitive $N$th root of unity, and a localization $\Lambda$ of $\mathbf Z[1/N,\zeta_N]$ over which $X,B$ and the action are defined, with $G$ trivial on $\Lambda$. Suppose a chart $a:Q\to M_B$ is given, with $Q$ sharp fs, and characters $\chi_Q:G_{\rm ab}\otimes Q^{\rm gp}\to\mu_N$ such that $g(a(q))=\chi_Q(g,q)a(q)$. Here $G_{\rm ab}$ is the quotient by commutators and $\mu_N$ is the group generated by $\zeta_N$.

After an equivariant pointed etale neighborhood [def-weil-etale-morphism] of $\bar x$, there are an fs monoid $P$ with torsion-free group of units, a homomorphism $\gamma:Q\to P$, a chart $b:P\to M_X$, and a character homomorphism $\chi_P:G_{\rm ab}\otimes P^{\rm gp}\to\mu_N$ extending $\chi_Q$, such that $g(b(p))=\chi_P(g,p)b(p)$ and $b\gamma=f^\flat a$. The map $\gamma^{\rm gp}$ is injective and the torsion subgroup of its cokernel is finite of order invertible near $\bar x$. The resulting comparison
$$X\longrightarrow B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[Q]}\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[P]$$
is strict, equivariant and smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Strict means that the log structure on its source is pulled back from its target; the monoid rings and fibre products are those of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale].

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, first and last assertions, printed pp.136--139 (the smooth comparison, before adjoining the representation).

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$, $S=\overline M_{X,\bar x}$, $C=S^{\rm gp}$ and $D=C/\operatorname{im}Q^{\rm gp}$. By [lem-per-very-tame-equivariant-sharp-chart], whose hypotheses (invertible order of the stabilizer $G$ and trivial action on $S$) are checked in Step 2, $S$ is a fine saturated sharp monoid; $Q$ is sharp fs by hypothesis. By [lem-trf-sharp-cone-lattice-intersection], applied to the sharp fs monoids $S$ and $Q$, both $C$ and $Q^{\rm gp}$ are finite free abelian groups. By [lem-per-log-cotangent-characteristic-quotient] choose classes $c_1,\ldots,c_r\in C$ whose images form a basis of $k\otimes D$; its map $\pi$ sends $d\log t_i$ to this basis for any lifts of these classes.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--139.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-very-tame-equivariant-sharp-chart] to $X$ at $\bar x$. Its hypotheses are exactly invertible inertia order and trivial action on $S$; it does not require log regularity or a trivial stratum action. Extend its sharp chart to group completions and lift $c_i$ to $t_i\in M_{X,\bar x}^{\rm gp}$ using that chart. Then $g(t_i)=\psi_i(g)t_i$ for characters of $G$. These characters take values in $\mu_N$: their orders divide the exponent of $G$, and [lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity] identifies the prime-to-residue-characteristic roots in the strict local ring with those generated by the chosen primitive root. All these roots are fixed by inertia, since their residues are fixed and distinct roots have distinct residues.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--139.

proof.text: Put $L=\mathbf Z^r\oplus Q^{\rm gp}$ and define $u:L\to M_{X,\bar x}^{\rm gp}$ by $u(e_i)=t_i$ and $u(q)=f^\flat a(q)$. This has eigencharacter $\psi$ extending $\chi_Q$. By [lem-per-log-cotangent-characteristic-quotient] the cokernel of $L\to C$ is finite killed by an integer $n$ invertible in $A$, and $A^\times$ is $n$-divisible. Apply [lem-per-divisible-unit-lattice-extension] to $B=M_{X,\bar x}^{\rm gp}$, its subgroup $A^\times$, and $u$. Obtain a finite free group $F$, an injection $i:L\hookrightarrow F$, a positive power $m$ of $n$ annihilating $F/iL$, and $v:F\to B$ extending $u$ and surjecting onto $C$. The required torsion-freeness of $B/A^\times=C$ was verified in Step 1.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--139.

proof.text: The extension $v$ is automatically an eigencharacter extension. For $a\in F$, triviality of the action on $C$ gives $z(g,a)=g(v(a))/v(a)\in A^\times$. Choose $l\in L$ with $ma=i(l)$. Then $z(g,a)^m=\psi(g,l)$, so $z(g,a)^{mN}=1$. The integer $mN$ is invertible in $A$. By [lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity], reduction is injective on these roots; inertia fixes their residues, hence fixes the roots themselves. The cocycle identity $z(gh,a)=g(z(h,a))z(g,a)$ now says that $g\mapsto z(g,a)$ is a character. Its exponent divides the exponent of $G$, so its values lie in $\mu_N$. Multiplicativity in $a$ gives $\chi_F:G_{\rm ab}\otimes F\to\mu_N$, extending $\psi$.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--139.

proof.text: Let $\bar v:F\twoheadrightarrow C$ be the characteristic map and $K=\ker\bar v$. Lift a finite basis of the free group $C$ to $F$, producing a section $s:C\to F$ and $F=K\oplus s(C)$. Since $F$ is finite free, [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free] makes $K$ finite free. Set $P=\bar v^{-1}(S)$. An element of $B=M_{X,\bar x}^{\rm gp}$ belongs to $M_{X,\bar x}$ exactly when its class in $C$ belongs to $S$: choose a monoid representative of that class and divide by it to obtain a unit. Thus $P=v^{-1}(M_{X,\bar x})$. The splitting identifies $P$ with $K\oplus S$. It is finitely generated by positive and negative basis elements of $K$ and lifts of generators of $S$, is integral, and is saturated because $S$ is saturated. Its units are $K$, hence torsion free, and $P^{\rm gp}=F$.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--139.

proof.text: The germ $v|_P$ is a chart. The map $P\oplus_K A^\times\to M_{X,\bar x}$ is onto because $\bar v(P)=S$. If $v(p)a=v(p^{\prime})a^{\prime}$, then $p-p^{\prime}\in K$ and the equality is exactly the pushout relation absorbing $v(p-p^{\prime})$ into the unit. This proves injectivity. Define $\gamma(q)=i(0,q)$; it lies in $P$ and $v\gamma=f^\flat a$. It is injective on group completions. The torsion of $F/Q^{\rm gp}$ injects into $F/iL$: its kernel lies in $iL/Q^{\rm gp}=\mathbf Z^r$, which is torsion free. Thus this torsion is finite killed by $m$. Every prime dividing its order divides $m$, hence is invertible near $\bar x$.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--139.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fine-log-stalk-chart-spreading] to $v|_P$, using Step 6, to extend this specified germ to a chart on a pointed etale neighbourhood $W$. Make it equivariant as follows. Take the finite fibre product over $X$ of all translates $gW$, pointed by the tuple of the chosen lifts. This is an etale neighbourhood by the finite limits assertion of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; permuting the factors gives a $G$-action fixing this tuple. Pull the chart from the identity factor. For a finite generating set of $P$ and $Q$, the equations $g(b(p))=\chi_F(g,p)b(p)$ and $b\gamma(q)=f^\flat a(q)$ hold at the selected stalk by Steps 4 and 6. The colimit definition of the stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] makes these finitely many equalities hold on a further pointed etale neighbourhood. Take the finite fibre product over the first product of all translates of this further neighbourhood. It has a $G$-action, an equivariant map to the first product, and a projection to the identity neighbourhood. Pulling the chart back along that equivariant map preserves every equation, since the identity projection factors through the neighbourhood where the equations hold. This gives an equivariant pointed etale chart. Relations follow from the monoid homomorphisms, so checking generators suffices.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--139.

proof.text: Let $Y=B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[Q]}\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[P]$, with its pulled-back chart log structure, and let $h=(f,b):W\to Y$. Restrict $Y$ to the open where $m$ is invertible and $W$ to its inverse image; these contain the selected points, because the local ring map at their images is local and $m$ is a unit in $A$. This restriction is invariant since $m$ is an integer. The equalities of Step 7 make this map equivariant. It is strict: pulling back the chart $P$ gives precisely the chart log structure of $W$, by [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]. The identity comparison for the chart $Q\to P$, with the injectivity and invertible torsion verified in Step 6, makes $Y\to B$ log smooth by [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Replacing the integral monoid rings by $\Lambda$-monoid rings makes no difference to the relative chart: $B$ is already a $\Lambda$-scheme and both fibre products identify with $B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--139.

proof.text: Compute $\omega_{Y/B}=\mathcal O_Y\otimes_{\mathbf Z}(F/Q^{\rm gp})$ directly from the differential relations. Over an affine of $B$, every regular function of $Y$ is a sum of base coefficients times monomials; the relation $d(z^p)=z^p d\log p$ eliminates their ordinary differentials. The remaining relations are exactly additivity in $P$ and $d\log\gamma(q)=0$. Conversely these formulas define a logarithmic derivation into the displayed tensor module, giving an inverse. Since $F/iL$ is killed by the invertible integer $m$, tensoring with $k$ identifies $k\otimes(F/Q^{\rm gp})$ with $k\otimes\mathbf Z^r$: an inverse sends $a\in F$ to $m^{-1}$ times the $\mathbf Z^r$ component of $ma\in iL$. The map to $k\otimes\omega_{W/B}$ sends its basis to $d\log t_i$. Composing with $\pi$ from Step 1 sends this basis to the chosen basis of $k\otimes D$, and is an isomorphism. Therefore the differential map itself is injective.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--139.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-strict-log-jacobian-criterion] to $h:W\to Y$ over $B$. The source is log smooth over $B$ by the hypothesis, the target is log smooth by Step 8, strictness is Step 8 and the required injectivity is Step 9. It gives an open neighbourhood on which the underlying $h$ is smooth. Intersect its finitely many $G$-translates; each restriction is smooth because equivariance identifies the translated map with the original one by automorphisms. This is still an invariant pointed etale neighbourhood. Restrict the chart to it. Together with Steps 4--8 this gives all the asserted properties, including torsion-free units and the prescribed base chart.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--139.
